`time`: time a command.

## Synopsis

<strong>time</strong> <em>command</em> \[<em>arg</em>...\]

## Description

<strong>time</strong> runs <em>command</em> with its arguments, waits for it, and then writes how long it took to standard error, after a blank line:

```text
real    0m1.250s
```

<em>command</em> is found as the shell finds it: a name with a <strong>/</strong> is a path, else the first match in <strong>PATH</strong>. It runs with <strong>time</strong>'s standard input, output and error.

## Exit status

The command's exit status; 128 + <em>n</em> if a signal <em>n</em> ended it; 127 if it isn't found; 126 if it can't be started; 2 (with a usage message) when no command is given.

## Notes

Only the real (elapsed) time is reported, from the computer's uptime: the kernel doesn't count user or system time. There are no options. It is a program, not a shell keyword, so it times one command, not a pipeline.

## See also

<strong>sh</strong>(1), <strong>uptime</strong>(1), <strong>sleep</strong>(1)
